subject: Civil Engineering
title: Tunnel Boring Machines
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Tunnel Boring Machines.

hook.text: A machine the length of 4 football fields chews through rock — creating a perfect tunnel behind it.

buildup.text: A TBM's rotating cutterhead grinds rock with tungsten carbide disc cutters at enormous force.

discovery.text: Behind the cutterhead, robotic arms install precast concrete segments — the tunnel lining.

twist.text: A TBM can't turn around — if it gets stuck, the entire project faces a crisis.

climax.text: Bertha, the world's largest TBM at 57 feet wide, dug Seattle's State Route 99 tunnel.

punchline.text: A billion-dollar worm that eats rock and leaves a finished tunnel in its wake.

quiz.question: What happens behind the TBM cutterhead as it advances?
options: Workers manually pour concrete to form the tunnel walls
Robotic arms install precast concrete segments to line the tunnel
The exposed rock is left unlined until the full tunnel is complete
